heroHeadline: Cité Soleil Residents Hold Public Protest Demanding Police Protection; MSF Hospital Day 19 of Closure; GSF Full Operations Launch June 1
heroSubtitle: On May 28, 2026, approximately two dozen residents of Cité Soleil — holding tree branches as symbols of defiance — gathered at a street intersection to demand police protection as gang violence continued for a fourth consecutive day, even as gunshots rang nearby. The Associated Press documented the scene firsthand: 67-year-old Roselaine Jean-Pierre, sleeping outdoors after fleeing her home, was among those demanding an end to violence that since May 25 has included mass shootings, arson of occupied homes with families inside, looting, and reported beheadings. MSF's hospital in Cité Soleil entered its 19th consecutive day of closure on May 28 — the longest documented uninterrupted shutdown since the crisis began — leaving approximately 300,000 commune residents without emergency medical access. Over 30,000 people have been newly displaced from Cité Soleil and surrounding Port-au-Prince areas since May 10, bringing the national IDP total to approximately 1.5 million. The Gang Suppression Force (GSF) full operations launch June 1 — three days away — but the ~800-person advance force (well below its 5,500-person authorized ceiling) remains exclusively deployed in Port-au-Prince's city center with no presence in Cité Soleil or the Artibonite. Separately, a United Nations News investigation published this week documents the collapse of Haiti's media ecosystem in gang-controlled zones: newsrooms shuttered, journalists silenced, and information voids exploited by gangs to suppress evidence of atrocities and prevent international accountability. The US Supreme Court ruling on TPS for ~350,000 Haitian nationals — in Noem v. Doe / Trump v. Miot — remains expected before late June 2026.
